title: BGP Basics: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: The internet is thousands of separate networks. Something has to tell them how to reach each other. That something is B G P.

lines.t: Who tells them how to connect?

scenes.heading: The postal service for the internet
scenes.narration: Think of the world's postal services swapping delivery routes. Each network has an autonomous system number. B G P peers talk over T C P port one seventy nine. Peers in different A S numbers are e B G P. Peers in the same A S number are i B G P.

scenes.heading: Basic setup
scenes.narration: A basic setup is short. Start B G P with your A S number. Name the neighbour and their A S. Advertise a network that exists exactly in your table. And check the summary.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. B G P only advertises what you ask it to. It uses T C P port one seventy nine. And active means it's still trying to connect.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. B G P connects separate networks, called autonomous systems. It uses T C P one seventy nine. e B G P is between A S numbers, and i B G P is inside one. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva BGP lab.

points.t: eBGP: between ASes. iBGP: inside one
